new.s: Where was the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana launched on 1 April 2017?
new.x: The Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana was launched at Nellore in Andhra Pradesh on 1 April 2017.

new.s: Which of the following is given free to BPL senior citizens under the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana?
o: Physical aids such as walking sticks, wheelchairs and hearing aids
10 kg of food grains a month
new.x: Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana gives free physical aids like walking sticks, wheelchairs, hearing aids and dentures to BPL seniors through ALIMCO.

new.s: Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY), launched in April 2021, was renamed from which earlier scheme?
o: National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly
National Action Plan for Senior Citizens
new.x: AVYAY was formed in April 2021 by renaming the National Action Plan for Senior Citizens.

new.s: What was the maximum purchase limit under the Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana after its revision in 2018?
new.x: PMVVY's maximum purchase limit was Rs 7.5 lakh at launch and was raised to Rs 15 lakh in 2018.

new.s: Who among the following is known as the first voter of independent India?
new.x: Shyam Saran Negi of Kalpa, Kinnaur (Himachal Pradesh) cast the first vote of independent India in October 1951.
new.angle: U0415 PYQ y476cdbb3615 Shyam Saran Negi -> first voter

new.s: Which State had the highest sex ratio as per Census 2011?
new.x: Kerala had the highest sex ratio in Census 2011 at 1084 females per 1000 males.

new.s: What was India's sex ratio as per Census 2011?
new.x: Census 2011 recorded India's sex ratio as 943 females per 1000 males.

new.s: Which State recorded the lowest sex ratio in Census 2011?
new.x: Haryana had the lowest sex ratio among States in Census 2011 at 879.

new.s: In which Census did agricultural labourers outnumber cultivators in India for the first time?
new.x: Census 2011 showed that the number of cultivators fell and agricultural labourers outnumbered cultivators for the first time.

new.s: Which State had the highest total fertility rate (TFR) as per NFHS-5?
new.x: NFHS-5 (2019-21) recorded Bihar's TFR as 3.0, the highest among States.

new.s: Which period of India's population growth is known as the phase of population explosion?
new.x: From 1951 to 1981 India's population grew at over 2% a year, so this period is called the population explosion phase.

new.s: Which State recorded the highest decadal population growth during 1991-2001?
new.x: Nagaland recorded the highest decadal growth (about 64%) in 1991-2001, while Kerala recorded the lowest.

new.s: Which was the second most populous State of India as per Census 2011?
new.x: In Census 2011 the order was Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and then West Bengal.

new.s: What percentage of reservation in all government services did Karnataka provide for transgender persons in July 2021?
new.x: In July 2021 Karnataka became the first State to give 1% reservation to transgender persons in all government services.
new.angle: U0417 #1/#11 First State with service quota

new.s: In NALSA v. Union of India (2014), what kind of reservation did the Supreme Court direct for transgender persons?
o: Vertical reservation by treating them as socially and educationally backward classes
new.x: NALSA directed that transgender persons be treated as SEBCs, giving a vertical, OBC-type quota; the community now demands horizontal reservation.

new.s: Which judges delivered the NALSA v. Union of India judgment on 15 April 2014?
o: Justices K.S. Radhakrishnan and A.K. Sikri
Justices D.Y. Chandrachud and S.K. Kaul
Justices J.S. Khehar and R.F. Nariman
Justices Dipak Misra and A.M. Khanwilkar
new.x: The NALSA judgment was delivered by Justices K.S. Radhakrishnan and A.K. Sikri.

new.s: In which case did the Supreme Court recognise transgender persons as the 'third gender'?
o: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
new.x: NALSA v. Union of India (2014) recognised transgender persons as the 'third gender' with self-determined gender identity.

new.s: Where was the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana for senior citizens launched in April 2017?
new.x: The Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana was launched on 1 April 2017 at Nellore, Andhra Pradesh.

new.s: Which State was the first to set up a Transgender Welfare Board, in 2008?
new.x: Tamil Nadu set up the Transgender Welfare Board in 2008; Karnataka gave the first job quota and Kerala framed the first policy.

new.s: Who became India's first openly transgender mayor, in Raigarh, Chhattisgarh, in 2015?
new.x: Madhu Bai Kinnar became the first openly transgender mayor at Raigarh in 2015.

new.s: Who was India's first transgender police sub-inspector?
new.x: K. Prithika Yashini of Tamil Nadu became the first transgender police sub-inspector.

new.s: Who nominates the Chairperson and Members of the National Commission for Minorities?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
new.x: The NCM's Chairperson and Members are nominated by the Central Government, not the President.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission for Minorities:
1. It is a constitutional body.
2. It has a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and five Members.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The NCM is a statutory body under the NCM Act, 1992, not a constitutional body; it has seven members including the Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson.
new.angle: U0418 #1/#10 NCM -> statutory status and composition

new.s: Which of the following statements about minority rights in India is correct?
o: Minority rights are absolute and cannot be regulated
Minority status is decided on an all-India basis
The State may regulate standards in minority institutions but cannot take away their management
Only religious minorities can set up educational institutions
new.x: Minority rights are not absolute: the State may regulate standards but cannot take away management; status is decided State-wise.
new.angle: U0418 PYQ y4cb695f657d minority rights not absolute

new.s: Which Article of the Constitution gives any section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture the right to conserve it?
new.x: Article 29(1) protects any section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture; it is not limited to minorities, unlike Article 30.

new.s: Where is the headquarters of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities?
new.x: The Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities, an office set up in 1957, has its headquarters at Prayagraj.
new.angle: U0418 #5/#17 Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (notes gap)

new.s: Which Article of the Constitution empowers the President to recognise a language spoken by a substantial part of a State's population?
new.x: Article 347 lets the President recognise a language spoken by a substantial part of a State's population.

new.s: Which is the second largest religious minority in India as per Census 2011?
new.x: Census 2011: Muslims 14.2% are the largest minority, followed by Christians 2.3% and Sikhs 1.7%.

new.s: What is the entry age for joining the Atal Pension Yojana?
new.x: The Atal Pension Yojana is open to people aged 18-40; only PMJJBY has an 18-50 entry age.

new.s: What monthly pension does the Atal Pension Yojana guarantee from the age of 60?
new.x: APY, run by PFRDA, gives a pension of Rs 1,000 to Rs 5,000 a month from age 60 depending on contribution.

new.s: Who was the chairman of the National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector (NCEUS), set up in 2004?
new.x: NCEUS was set up in 2004 under Arjun Sengupta; it found 77% of Indians living on under Rs 20 a day.

new.s: Up to what monthly income can unorganised workers join the PM Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM) scheme?
new.x: PM-SYM is for unorganised workers aged 18-40 earning up to Rs 15,000 a month.
